title: Si: Ion-cut donor reuse, one prime wafer feeds ten DRAM wafers
idea: Hydrogen-implant and cleave (Smart-Cut) the top 1-2 um of a prime CZ silicon wafer onto a cheap reclaimed or polysilicon carrier, then CMP and re-epi the donor and reuse it 10+ times, because DRAM arrays only use the top few microns.
why: Cuts CZ ingot growth, and so Spruce Pine quartz-crucible demand, per DRAM wafer by ~5-10x; turns a binary chokepoint into a small-volume one.

title: O: Synthetic sol-gel silica crucibles from polysilicon-plant SiCl4 waste
idea: Hydrolyze the SiCl4 byproduct of Siemens polysilicon plants into ultra-pure sol-gel/fumed silica, slip-cast and arc-fuse it into fully synthetic CZ crucibles (bubble-free inner wall, nucleated outer wall), qualified in a U.S. plant.
why: Breaks the >80% Spruce Pine high-purity-quartz dependence for crucibles while converting a waste stream into feedstock; secures U.S. wafer supply for DRAM.

title: He: Helium-recapture-as-a-service skids leased per fab bay
idea: A third party installs membrane plus cryo-adsorption helium recovery skids on chuck backside-cooling, leak-check and purge exhausts, owns the gas, re-purifies it to 6N on site and sells the fab guaranteed helium availability at a fixed price per wafer start.
why: 70-90% less virgin helium; converts the Qatar outage chokepoint into a service contract with no fab capex.

title: H: Electrolytic hydrogen replaces helium as electrostatic-chuck backside gas
idea: Use on-site PEM-electrolyzed H2 (thermal conductivity 0.18 vs 0.15 W/mK for He) as the low-pressure backside cooling gas in etch and deposition chucks, with leak sensing and dilution exhaust, and deuterium blends where plasma chemistry requires.
why: Eliminates the largest helium use in DRAM fabs using only water and electricity, available anywhere.

title: N: Cryo-binning resurrects retention-rejected DRAM dies in liquid nitrogen
idea: Dies and aging modules that fail 64 ms retention at 85 C because of the junction-leakage tail retain for seconds at 77 K; grade them by cold retention and sell them into LN2-cooled cold-memory sleds where refresh is nearly turned off.
why: Converts several percent of yield loss and retired modules into usable supply and cuts refresh energy >90% in that tier.

title: Mo: Climax molybdenum replaces Chinese tungsten in DRAM wordlines
idea: Switch buried-wordline fill and bitline contacts from WF6-CVD tungsten to barrierless MoO2Cl2/MoCl5-CVD molybdenum under long-term offtake from Colorado's Climax and Henderson mines plus a U.S. precursor plant.
why: Removes most exposure to ~80% China tungsten supply; barrierless Mo also lowers narrow-line wordline RC ~20-30%.

title: Al: Shuttered aluminum smelters become fast-track memory fab sites
idea: Acquire idled aluminum smelter sites whose 300-700 MW firm grid interconnects, industrial water permits, rail spurs and heavy-industry zoning already exist, and drop in modular back-end first, then front-end shells.
why: Grid queues and permitting are 2-4 years of fab lead time; reuse cuts time-to-bits by ~1-2 years and avoids grid capex.

title: Fe: Iron-air multi-day batteries let fabs sit on stranded wind
idea: Pair a memory fab with 100-hour iron-air batteries (reversible rusting of iron pellets) plus a fast flywheel ride-through layer so it can site in curtailed-wind regions with fab-grade power quality.
why: Stranded power at ~$15-25/MWh versus $60-80 roughly halves fab electricity cost and opens sites with no grid upgrade.

title: Zn: Indium-free zinc-tin-oxide gain cells built in idle LCD fabs
idea: Retool depreciated Gen-6/8 display lines to make ZTO (Zn, Sn, O only; no In or Ga) 2T0C gain-cell DRAM on glass at ~1 um rules, stacking a few layers; one Gen-8 panel yields ~100 GB per layer, diced into CXL capacity-tier tiles.
why: Glass panel area is ~100x cheaper per m2 than 300 mm wafer area and needs no EUV; avoids In/Ga chokepoints; a capacity tier at a few $/GB.

title: Ti: Rutile TiO2 on tin-oxide seed breaks the capacitor charge wall
idea: Replace ZrO2-based capacitor dielectrics with rutile TiO2 (k ~80-100) crystallized at low temperature on an isostructural rutile SnO2 seed instead of scarce RuO2, with Ti precursor from U.S. ilmenite sands.
why: k ~90 meets the fact-sheet k~70 target, allowing ~40:1 instead of 75:1 pillars (cheaper etch, more cell headroom) and less Hf/Zr reliance.

title: C: Diamond-like-carbon nanoimprint masters replace EUV on array layers
idea: Coat quartz nanoimprint templates with a ta-C/DLC wear layer to extend template life ~10x, then imprint the strictly periodic DRAM array layers (active, buried wordline, storage node) while DUV handles periphery.
why: Removes 3-5 EUV exposures per wafer at ~1/10 tool cost and power, and breaks the single-supplier EUV dependence.

title: Na/Cl: Salt-cavern strategic helium reserve for semiconductor fabs
idea: Store purified helium in leached Gulf Coast salt caverns, as done for oil and hydrogen, funded by a per-wafer industry levy, with automatic release triggers on supply shocks like the 2026 Qatar outage.
why: Replaces the privatized Federal Helium Reserve; buffers 1-2 years of U.S. semiconductor helium demand.

title: Sn: Bismuth-tin low-temperature reballing harvests DRAM from retired servers
idea: An automated line desolders DRAM packages from retired DIMMs and boards below 170 C with Bi-Sn solder and laser selective reflow, tests each die for retention and hammer threshold, reballs and remounts them as graded modules.
why: Hyperscalers retire exabyte-scale DRAM after 4-6 years; harvesting 30% of it adds several percent to annual supply at near-zero capital.

title: Ca: CaF2-optic DUV forever-node lines from refurbished scanners
idea: Freeze a DRAM design at an EUV-free 1z-class node with self-aligned quadruple patterning, buy used ArF-immersion scanners on the secondary market and refurbish their CaF2 optics domestically, competing on depreciated capital rather than node.
why: Nodes buy only 10-20% cost/bit while depreciation is ~55% of wafer cost; fully depreciated DUV lines win $/bit for capacity tiers.

title: S: On-site sulfuric acid regeneration makes memory micro-fabs portable
idea: A containerized unit distills and re-oxidizes spent piranha H2SO4 and electrolytically generates peroxide on site, closing the chemical loop so a 5k wafer-per-month micro-fab needs no bulk acid logistics.
why: ~90% less acid purchase and waste; removes chemical supply chain and permitting barriers to siting small memory fabs.

title: Cu: LME-style physically delivered DRAM futures to finance capacity
idea: Create a standardized, warehouse-receipt DRAM futures contract (16 Gb die-equivalents in bonded vaults) modeled on LME copper and aluminum, so buyers hedge 3-5 years ahead and fabs borrow against forward sales.
why: A 4x price swing deters capex; a hedgeable forward curve lowers cost of capital for new fabs by several points.

title: Au: Gold-finger DIMM deposit-refund law drives memory take-back
idea: Levy a $3-10 refundable deposit per DIMM/SODIMM, like bottle bills, redeemable at certified harvesters whose gold-finger and DRAM resale value fund the program and feed reballing lines.
why: Raises end-of-life memory return rates from <20% toward 70%, creating a steady secondary DRAM supply.

title: Ge: Shared silicon-germanium superlattice epi foundry for 3D DRAM
idea: A U.S. epi-as-a-service foundry grows 30-100-tier Si/SiGe superlattices, the starting stack for lateral 3D DRAM, on customer wafers using SiGe BiCMOS epi know-how, so new entrants need no epi capex.
why: 3D DRAM needs 26+ tiers and epi uniformity is a bottleneck; pooled tools cut entry capital and accelerate many 3D DRAM teams.

title: W: Closed-loop WF6 recovery from CVD exhaust and target scrap
idea: Cryotrap unreacted WF6 from CVD exhaust (typical utilization 20-30%) and re-fluorinate tungsten chamber scrapings and sputter-target remnants back to WF6 in an on-site loop.
why: Cuts virgin tungsten demand ~50-70% in a supply chain ~80% controlled by China.

title: Zr: Open-source zirconia trench-capacitor DRAM PDK for U.S. foundries
idea: Publish an open PDK and macro compiler for a ZrO2/TiN deep-trench 1T1C DRAM cell on 130-90 nm U.S. foundries, so defense, auto and industrial buyers source companion DRAM domestically.
why: Mature fabs cost ~1/20th of leading-edge; moves legacy demand off scarce leading-edge bits and seeds U.S. DRAM skills.

title: Ar: Industrial-gas cooperative utility for a memory micro-fab park
idea: Cluster 4-8 memory micro-fabs around one cooperatively owned air-separation unit (N2, Ar, O2), shared helium recovery and ultrapure-water plant, each fab paying by metered consumption.
why: Utilities are ~20-30% of fab capex; sharing makes 5-10k wafer-per-month memory fabs economically viable.

title: K: KOH crystallographic etch digs ultra-high-aspect capacitor trenches
idea: On (110) silicon, anisotropic KOH/TMAH etching exposes vertical {111} sidewalls with >100:1 rate selectivity, so hardmask-defined trenches reach AR >100 on cheap wet benches instead of cryogenic plasma HAR etchers.
why: Fact #1 needs AR ~115; wet benches cost ~1/10 of HAR etch tools and relieve the etch-tool bottleneck.

title: Ce: Closed-loop ceria CMP slurry recovery cuts rare-earth exposure
idea: Recover CeO2 abrasive from spent STI/ILD CMP slurry by flocculation, acid leach and recalcination, and qualify blended ceria-silica slurries using half the cerium.
why: China dominates rare-earth cerium refining; recycling and dilution cut a hidden chokepoint in DRAM CMP.

title: Mg: Retool HDD read-head fabs as MgO tunnel-junction memory foundries
idea: HDD head fabs already sputter and pattern CoFeB/MgO tunnel junctions below 30 nm; as hard-drive unit volumes fall, convert these lines to STT-MRAM back-end processing on foundry-supplied CMOS wafers.
why: Adds non-volatile 10-30 ns memory capacity using existing tools and staff, avoiding a ~$10B greenfield fab.

title: Hf: Dielectric-swap kit converts legacy DRAM fabs to FeRAM
idea: Depreciated 2x-3x nm DRAM fabs swap their ZrO2 capacitor dielectric for Si- or Zr-doped ferroelectric HfO2 in the same cylinders, add plate-line drivers and new sense timing, and make 1T1C FeRAM; Hf comes from U.S. nuclear-zirconium refining byproduct.
why: Non-volatile, refresh-free DRAM-class memory from fabs with near-zero new capital.

title: Fe: Fe/Cr coupled antiferromagnet removes iridium and ruthenium from MRAM
idea: Replace Ru-spacer synthetic antiferromagnets and IrMn/PtMn pinning in MTJ stacks with Fe/Cr interlayer-coupled multilayers and a high-anisotropy Fe-based reference layer.
why: Ir and Ru are among the scarcest elements; removing them lets non-volatile MRAM scale to commodity volume.

title: N: Idled 3D-NAND fabs build gain cells with charge-trap backup tiers
idea: In one 3D NAND staircase stack, form vertical-channel gain-cell tiers as working memory next to SiN charge-trap tiers; on power-loss detect an on-die capacitor bank streams the gain-cell contents into the charge-trap tiers.
why: Uses underutilized NAND capacity for non-volatile-backed DRAM-class memory; NAND endurance is spent only at shutdown.

title: C: Coconut-carbon supercaps turn harvested DIMMs into persistent memory
idea: Retrofit kits pair second-life DIMMs with activated-carbon supercapacitors (coconut-shell carbon) plus a small NAND and controller that saves the DRAM image on power loss, sold as an Optane-replacement persistent tier.
why: Makes reused DRAM non-volatile and more valuable, improving harvest economics; no lithium or cobalt.

title: Al: U.S. BAW-filter fabs make aluminum-boron-nitride ferroelectric memory
idea: RF BAW filter fabs already sputter piezoelectric AlN at volume; adding boron co-sputtering yields wurtzite Al(1-x)B(x)N ferroelectric (Pr >100 uC/cm2) capacitors and FeFETs as a BEOL non-volatile memory.
why: Abundant Al, B, N replace scarce Sc of AlScN and reuse existing U.S. sputter capacity; huge Pr allows tiny cells.

title: Zn: Tellurium-free zinc-antimonide phase-change memory from Idaho antimony
idea: Use Zn-Sb phase-change alloys (fast, high crystallization temperature) instead of GeSbTe in crosspoint storage-class memory, sourcing antimony from Idaho's Stibnite deposit.
why: Te is a ~500 t/yr byproduct and Ge is China-concentrated; Zn-Sb gives non-volatile memory from abundant-to-domestic elements.

title: Ti: TiOx ReRAM weight vault evicts static AI weights from DRAM
idea: Store frozen model weights in dense non-volatile TiOx ReRAM on an accelerator side-die with on-die dequantization; weights are written only at deployment, so DRAM/HBM holds only KV cache and activations.
why: Weights are ~50-80% of inference memory footprint; moving them frees that DRAM supply and its refresh energy.

title: Si: DLP micromirror fabs build bistable nano-cantilever memory
idea: Scale the digital-micromirror MEMS process (Al hinges proven beyond 10^12 cycles) down to sub-100 nm Si/Al cantilevers that latch against contacts by adhesion and are read capacitively.
why: Reuses existing U.S. MEMS fabs with no new materials; zero standby power, no leakage tail, radiation hard.

title: O: Atmospheric spatial-ALD micro-fabs for ferroelectric oxide memory
idea: Vacuum-free spatial-ALD heads deposit HZO and oxide electrodes at ~10x throughput on mature-foundry 200 mm CMOS wafers, finishing a FeRAM BEOL in a $50-100M micro-fab.
why: Distributed non-volatile memory manufacturing at ~1/50th the capital of a DRAM fab.

title: Na: Sodium-ion rack batteries make DRAM durable, deleting database replicas
idea: Rack-level Na-ion batteries hold servers up long enough to flush DRAM to NVMe on power loss, certified as durable, so in-memory databases and caches drop one of their 2-3 durability replicas.
why: Saves 33-50% of DRAM in replicated in-memory clusters; Na-ion avoids Li and Co.

title: S: Sulfide self-selecting crosspoint memory without tellurium or arsenic
idea: Build selector-only memory from Ge-S or Si-Ge-S-N sulfide chalcogenides whose polarity-dependent threshold shift stores a bit, stacked as 4F2 crosspoint decks in BEOL; sulfur comes from refinery byproduct.
why: Te/Se/As-free non-volatile crosspoint at ~10-50 ns, density 4F2 divided by deck count.

title: Cu: Copper conductive-bridge memory released as zero-new-material open IP
idea: Release royalty-free CBRAM IP that uses a fab's own Cu BEOL and SiCN/SiO2 dielectric as the switching electrolyte, adding one mask and no new tools.
why: Every Cu-BEOL logic fab becomes a non-volatile memory supplier for persistence and capacity tiers.

title: Mn: Iridium-free Mn3Sn antiferromagnetic memory built on MRAM lines
idea: Store bits in the chiral spin order of Mn3Sn, switched by spin-orbit torque and read through its large anomalous Hall or tunnel signal; no stray fields lets cells pack at sub-20 nm pitch.
why: Abundant Mn and Sn, picosecond switching potential, no Ir/Pt/Co, denser than MRAM.

title: Cr: Chromia magnetoelectric memory written by voltage, not current
idea: Boron-doped Cr2O3 films (Neel temperature raised above 400 K) flip their boundary magnetization with an electric field plus small bias field, read by anomalous Hall in an adjacent Fe layer.
why: Voltage writes cost ~100x less energy than STT; chromium is abundant and recyclable from stainless steel.

title: Zr: Hafnium-free zirconia antiferroelectric with built-in bias stores bits
idea: Put pure antiferroelectric ZrO2 between electrodes of different work function so the built-in field shifts the double hysteresis loop, leaving two stable remanent states at zero volts.
why: Zr is far more abundant than scarce Hf; reuses DRAM ZrO2 ALD tools; antiferroelectric endurance beats ferroelectric.

title: Te: Optane afterlife market redeploys stranded 3D XPoint persistent memory
idea: Buy back stranded and retired Intel Optane PMem inventory, re-certify endurance, and resell it with open-source firmware and driver support to tier-2 clouds as a persistent memory pool.
why: Zero-capital non-volatile capacity that displaces DRAM in memory-mode deployments.

title: Li: Lithium-niobate photonics wafer lines make domain-wall memory
idea: Thin-film LiNbO3-on-insulator wafers, now mass-produced for modulators, host ferroelectric domain-wall memory where a written conducting wall bridges two electrodes and is read nondestructively in nanoseconds.
why: Non-volatile, nondestructive read and high endurance, reusing a fast-growing wafer supply chain.

title: Bi: Bismuth-antimony topological SOT-MRAM from HDD reader know-how
idea: Use sputtered BiSb, with a record spin Hall angle developed for HDD readers, as the spin-orbit-torque write line in MRAM instead of W, Ta or Pt.
why: ~10x lower write current than W-based SOT and avoids China-dominated tungsten and platinum.

title: Ni: Electroplated permalloy racetrack memory from HDD write-pole plating lines
idea: Electroplate NiFe nanowires into deep trenches like HDD write poles to form vertical racetrack shift registers holding 10-100 domain-wall bits read by one sensor at the top.
why: Electroplating costs ~1/10 the capex of vacuum deposition and gives many non-volatile bits per footprint.

title: Ga: Abundance-screened bill-of-materials procurement rule for memory
idea: Learning from China's 2023 gallium and germanium export controls, a federal procurement rule scores memory by mass-weighted element supply concentration and gives price preference to non-volatile memories built only from abundant elements.
why: Steers demand and venture money toward chokepoint-free non-volatile memory, cutting systemic supply risk.

title: U: Uranium-style take-or-pay contracts finance new non-volatile memory fabs
idea: Like utilities buying enrichment a decade ahead, hyperscalers sign 7-10-year take-or-pay contracts for MRAM/FeRAM wafer output at indexed prices, letting startups finance fabs with project debt.
why: Cuts cost of capital from ~20% equity to ~8% debt for a non-volatile memory industry that lacks scale.

title: H: Croconic-acid hydrogen-bond ferroelectric memory from carbon, hydrogen, oxygen
idea: Croconic acid (C5H2O5) switches polarization by proton transfer along hydrogen bonds (Pr ~20-30 uC/cm2 at room temperature); evaporate it below 150 C onto any CMOS BEOL as non-volatile capacitors.
why: Fully abundant C, H, O and a low-temperature process enable distributed manufacturing.
